neet_phy_u20_t12_1.working: No parallax means the pin tip and the image tip move together as the eye shifts sideways. That happens only when they are at the same location.

neet_phy_u20_t12_2.working: Index correction = 20.0 − 19.6 = +0.4 cm. Corrected u = v = 29.6 + 0.4 = 30.0 cm. A same-size image means u = v = 2f, so f = 15.0 cm.

neet_phy_u20_t12_3.working: Corrected distance = 23.5 + 0.5 = 24.0 cm. This equals the radius of curvature R of the mirror, so f = R/2 = 12.0 cm.

neet_phy_u20_t12_4.working: A convex mirror forms only a virtual image of a real object, so no image pin can be placed on that image. This is why an auxiliary convex lens is needed. Both statements are true and R explains A.

neet_phy_u20_t12_5.working: Statement I: the u-v graph is a rectangular hyperbola. Using magnitudes, 1/u + 1/v = 1/f, so the 1/v vs 1/u graph is a straight line with both intercepts equal to 1/f. Statement II: a same-size real image forms when the object is at the centre of curvature, i.e. at a distance of 2f. Both are correct.
